title: Understanding Wills in India: Definition & Importance

faq.q: Can a Will be challenged in India?
faq.a: Yes, a Will can be challenged in court on grounds such as lack of proper execution, undue influence, fraud, or the testator's unsound mind. However, a well-drafted and registered Will is more difficult to challenge successfully.

faq.q: Is it mandatory to register a Will in India?
faq.a: No, registration of a Will is not mandatory under Indian law. An unregistered Will is as legally valid as a registered one, provided it meets all other legal requirements. However, registration is highly recommended as it adds authenticity and makes it harder to dispute.

faq.q: What is the role of an executor in a Will?
faq.a: An executor is the person appointed in the Will to carry out the testator's wishes. Their responsibilities include obtaining probate (if required), collecting assets, paying off debts, and distributing the remaining estate to the beneficiaries as per the Will.

faq.q: Can a Non-Resident Indian (NRI) make a Will for their Indian assets?
faq.a: Yes, an NRI can absolutely make a Will for their assets located in India. It is highly advisable for NRIs to have a separate Will for their Indian assets to simplify the inheritance process and avoid conflicts with succession laws of their country of residence.

faq.q: What happens if I acquire more assets after making a Will?
faq.a: Generally, a Will should contain a 'residuary clause' which dictates how any assets not specifically mentioned, including those acquired after the Will's creation, should be distributed. If there's no such clause, these new assets might be distributed as per intestate succession laws. It's best to update your Will or add a Codicil.

faq.q: Is a Will expensive to make in India?
faq.a: The cost of making a Will can vary. A simple, self-drafted Will might cost nothing, but engaging a lawyer for a comprehensive, legally sound Will could range from a few thousand rupees to ₹15,000-₹20,000 or more, depending on the complexity of the estate and the lawyer's fees.

faq.q: Can I change my Will after it has been made?
faq.a: Yes, a Will is a revocable document and can be changed or updated any number of times during the testator's lifetime, provided they are of sound mind. Changes can be made through a Codicil (for minor alterations) or by drafting an entirely new Will (which should explicitly revoke all previous Wills).
